key_insight: Train a Vision Transformer to speak directly by predicting language tokens from visual tokens with a standard autoregressive language-modeling objective, removing the need for contrastive setups or extra text decoders. This aligns vision encoders naturally with LLMs for generative multimodal models.
problem_solved: Bridges the modality gap between visual encoders and autoregressive language models by removing complex contrastive pretraining and auxiliary text decoders, simplifying pretraining while improving compatibility with multimodal LLMs.
method: Use a ViT to encode visual tokens and directly predict subsequent language tokens using an autoregressive language modeling loss.
Eschew contrastive batch construction and separate text-decoder modules — rely on a minimalist, generative pretraining objective.
Design the training pipeline so the ViT can be plugged into or integrated with multimodal LLMs for end-to-end generative tasks.
impact: Provides a simpler, more direct route to build generative multimodal models that integrate ViTs with LLMs, reducing engineering complexity and pretraining overhead while improving alignment for downstream multimodal generation and understanding.

paper_title: Let ViT Speak: Generative Language-Image Pre-training
